title: Antisocial Theatergoers
statementMd:
Laila is going to the theater to see a performance by Clube da Esquina, a celebrated Brazilian musical collective. Unfortunately, something has come up, and she will be the last person to arrive.

The theater has a single row of 𝑛n seats, numbered from 11 to 𝑛n, with an aisle at each end. The aisles are represented by positions 00 and 𝑛+1n+1. The distance between positions 𝑖i and 𝑗j is |𝑖−𝑗||i−j|.

The show is sold out. The 𝑛−1n−1 people arriving before Laila enter one at a time and are extremely antisocial: each wants to sit as far as possible from both the people already seated and the aisles.

The **comfort** of an empty seat is the minimum distance from that seat to any occupied seat or aisle, measured when the person chooses their seat. Each person chooses an empty seat with **maximum comfort**. If several seats tie, they may choose any of them.

On her way to the theater, Laila can think of only one thing: which seat will be left for her?

For each seat 𝑘k, from 11 to 𝑛n, determine how many sequences of choices by the 𝑛−1n−1 people leave that seat empty. Two sequences are different if the seat chosen at some step differs. Since the answers may be large, print each answer modulo 998244353998244353.

## Input

The input consists of a single line containing an integer 𝑛n (2≤𝑛≤1052≤n≤105), the number of seats.

## Output

Print 𝑛n space-separated integers on a single line. The 𝑘k-th integer must be the number of valid sequences of choices that leave seat 𝑘k as the last available seat, modulo 998244353998244353.

## Note

**Explanation for example 1**

The first person chooses seat 22. The second may choose seat 11 or 33, leaving the other empty. Thus, the answers are 11, 00, and 11.
